thread:
incident-bot: [pagerduty] CRITICAL: redis-core acceptqueue saturation triggered for service redis-core
pagerduty: PagerDuty incident PD12345 created — paging eng-oncall (urgent). https://pagerduty.mock/incidents/PD12345
arjun: Acked. I'm on it — checking redis metrics and pgbouncer.
leo: thanks. tagging @arjun @maria in case this needs DB changes.
arjun: quick snapshot from the edge (running redis INFO clients):
```
connected_clients:1020
blocked_clients:118
client_recent_max_input_buffer:2048
client_recent_max_output_buffer:1024
maxclients:1000
```
arjun: blocked_clients > 0 and connected_clients > maxclients -> clients are being queued at accept layer. this matches 5xxs in the api.
sara: confirmed: traces show 503s and long queue times for the embedding requests. approx 10-15% of production traffic affected (some customer-facing timeouts).
maria: any recent deploy or job spike?
arjun: looking at cron/history — there's a new async batch job that started ~01:12 UTC (bulk rehydrate cache) — looks like it opened lots of persistent connections to redis without pooling.
leo: oh that job was rolled out yesterday to speed up warmups. might be the culprit.
arjun: mitigation plan: 1) pause the rehydrate job 2) temporarily raise redis maxclients and pgbouncer pool as a stopgap 3) throttle job and fix connection pooling in the job code 4) monitor for regressions / handoff
sara: impact note: frontend timeouts for some orgs hitting embeddings endpoints. will draft external note if we need longer mitigation.
arjun: pausing job now (k8s):
```bash
kubectl -n batch annotate job/bulk-rehydrate pause=true --overwrite
```
arjun: paused. verifying accept queue: `ss -ntlp | grep redis` shows acceptq dropping, blocked_clients climbing down.
arjun: pgbouncer shows a lot of waiters; increasing pool sizing as temporary measure.
```
# pgbouncer stats (snip)
active: 870
waiting: 210
total_clients: 1085
max_client_conn: 1200
```
maria: can we also bump redis maxclients? ops?
leo: doing a redis config update on the replica group now — pushing `maxclients 2000` to the cluster (will roll one node at a time).
leo: update: node-3 applied, connections accepted increased. watch for memory OOM.
arjun: note: this is a stopgap — increasing maxclients can increase memory usage per-connection; we should not rely on it long term.
sara: observed error rate falling from ~12% -> 3% in the last 4 minutes after pause + pgbouncer bump. good signal.
pagerduty: PD12345: Escalation scheduled in 10m if not resolved.
arjun: I'm going to instrument a quick rate limit at the gate for embedding endpoints to protect backend while we fix the job. applying a 50rps per-org soft throttle.
arjun: deploying rate-limit config:
```yaml
- route: /v1/embeddings
  rate_limit: 50
  scope: org
```
leo: SA acknowledged, monitoring.
maria: starting to compile action items for postmortem: root cause = noisy async job + lack of connection pooling + insufficient guardrails on max open connections.
sara: customer impact estimate: peak: ~12% requests affected, mostly latency/timeouts for embeddings and rerank features, ~6 customers with errors visible in dashboards.
arjun: rolling fix for job in progress (switch to pooled client using our shared connection library). pushing a patch to batch-service.
arjun: patch applied to image tag batch-service:fix/conn-pool-2026 -> redeploying via canary 10%
maria: if canary looks good, roll to 100% and re-run a sampled rehydrate to validate.
arjun: canary ok at 10% after 3 mins, connections stable. ramping to 50%.
sara: metrics: blocked_clients -> 10, connected_clients -> 420, 5xx -> 1.2%
leo: rolling redis config back to safer `maxclients: 1100` on nodes that already moved, leaving the surge node at 2000 for now.
leo: also opened an autoscaling ticket to add connection-based autoscaling to redis proxy layer.
arjun: preparing handoff — I'll stick on call for another 20m then hand to @maria unless it regresses. if anything spikes re-page PD.
maria: taking handoff at 02:00 UTC. summary: paused noisy job, temp pgbouncer bump, one redis node scaled to higher maxclients, rate limit on embeddings, job patched to use pooled connections. current status: degraded -> recovering.
sara: drafting customer comms template in #support_incidents; will coordinate if we need to notify customers.
pagerduty: PD12345: Acknowledged by arjun. No further escalation scheduled while assigned.
maria: postmortem owner: arjun + maria. next steps: revert redis maxclients to safe value after full validation, add circuit breaker on rehydrate job, hard quota on open redis connections in batch cluster, add alert for blocked_clients > 30 for 3m.
arjun: will follow up with PRs for guardrails and add an eval to Redwood Optimize to detect these kinds of spikes in cache rehydrate patterns.
maria: handing over — thanks everyone, posting handoff notes to incidents channel.
arjun: thanks — leaving thread in case follow-ups are needed. :thumbsup:
